correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and east-to-west upper course
correspondence.finding: The selected mainstem begins with a northward headward interval and a substantial westward course before turning north. Neither inspected source supplies continuous channel cartography for this chosen opening and upper connection. A regional Santiago basin description cannot establish that route or assign an upstream component name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward eastern mainstem arc and join into the westbound middle fragment
correspondence.finding: The regional sources identify Santiago in the eastern drainage setting. The municipal hydrography map shades basin areas rather than tracing the full chosen watercourse. The long selected arc and its fragment join therefore remain unestablished at ordinary through-corridor scale; the model connection is not substituted for primary evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Westbound middle mainstem toward the Santiago–Cayapas junction setting
correspondence.finding: OAS describes Santiago turning west after Concepción and a Santiago–Cayapas meeting at Borbón. Municipal maps locate Maldonado and Borbón. These anchors support a bounded Santiago candidate, but no inspected source traces the whole selected westbound connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southwestern tributary opening and northward approach
correspondence.finding: The selected side branch lies in the Cayapas-side setting. The municipal map separately depicts the Cayapas and Ónzole basin areas; OAS keeps those river identities distinct. Neither source establishes the chosen tributary opening and complete onward channel. Cayapas remains a bounded component candidate, not a confirmed name for every selected segment.

correspondence.component_scope: Tributary fragment join and approach to the shared lower mainstem
correspondence.finding: The sources support a Santiago–Cayapas receiving relationship in the Borbón region. The join between the two selected tributary fragments and its subsequent arrival at the mainstem are not independently traced by the inspected basin-area and settlement maps.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern lower fragment and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selection ends on the northward lower extension beyond the common junction. Municipal mapping supplies the northern coastal/estuarine regional setting, but depicts no continuous named channel to the selected ending. The endpoint is not silently moved to the outer Pacific coast or a neighboring estuarine branch. This is a through-connection evidence gap, not a requirement to establish an exact modern bank or mouth vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Waterbody or managed connectors
correspondence.finding: No selected lake, reservoir, glacier or managed connector is established by the material actually read. Their absence is not independently certified; no waterbody name or hydraulic operation is inferred from model continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and initial northward and westward bends
correspondence.finding: The opening lies by La Esperanza south of Nuevo Xcán. Through Nuevo Xcán, X-Can, Xim-Há and San Andrés, the selected alignment crosses mapped land and road corridors without a corresponding drawn continuous watercourse. No opening river name or subsurface through-link is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Interior continuation and approach to northern wetlands
correspondence.finding: The path continues through the San José de Montecristo–Colonia Yucatán–Samaria–Santa María setting. Local waterbodies, roads and vegetation are mapped, but no continuous river follows the chosen inland bends. Their connection to the coastal wetland remains unproved.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern wetland turn and lagoon approach
correspondence.finding: Near El Colorado and Moctezuma the selected route reaches inundation-prone terrain, turns northwest through the Laguna Larga setting, and enters the Laguna Flamingos coastal-waterbody setting. The mapped wetland footprint does not establish a through-going river or the inland connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Coastal estero and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The western selected coastal passage corresponds to the mapped Estero Río Lagartos water-and-wetland corridor across the sheet seam. Salina las Coloradas and connecting roads are separately depicted. The actual endpoint remains inside the estuarine setting east of San Felipe; it is not a demonstrated Gulf-mouth point. The nearby Río Lagartos town label is distinct from the estero label.
correspondence.candidate_name_role: Bounded downstream estuarine-waterbody component; not a whole-river or whole-system name

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern selected opening in the Huacraruco corridor, west through the San Juan reach and its downstream junction setting.
correspondence.finding: The original hydrographic line covers the selected eastern opening and westward Huacraruco course, its Pacachal-side junction, San Juan reach and continuation into the Magdalena valley. It separates the southern Paigual/Grande/Asunción branch and northern Chotén/Naranjo tributaries from the selected through-route. The report explicitly describes the Huacraruco–San Juan–Magdalena sequence.
correspondence.name_scope: Huacraruco and San Juan remain bounded reach names; the selected opening is not asserted to be the report’s ultimate spring or source lagoon.

correspondence.component_scope: Magdalena valley through the town of Magdalena to the Chilete junction setting.
correspondence.finding: The inspected map traces the northwestward Magdalena course and connected westward reach, with the Chetillano and Chanta joins, through to Chilete. San Pablo enters from the north and Huertas from the south at the Chilete setting; the selected course continues west.
correspondence.name_scope: Magdalena is a reach name, with Chilete used downstream of the junction setting; no precise name-transition vertex assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Chilete westward course, Contumazá and San Miguel junctions, broad northern bend and southward turn to Yonán.
correspondence.finding: The original map continuously shows the selected westward Chilete line, the southern Contumazá contribution, and the San Miguel/Puglush receiving junction before the Jequetepeque-labeled reach. The western bend then turns south and west into the Yonán setting. The report’s named river sequence and SENAMHI hydrologic prose support this connected main-river identity.
correspondence.name_scope: Jequetepeque is the downstream representative name. The map/report use San Miguel for the northern tributary; SENAMHI also uses Puclush in the confluence description.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected river corridor from the Yonán/Tembladera approach through the Gallito Ciego reservoir and its western downstream connection.
correspondence.finding: Map5 traces the selected river-valley through-link. C36 printed pages9 and21 place the Gallito Ciego reservoir on the Jequetepeque bed from below Tembladera to Gallito Ciego. SENAMHI Figure3-1 visibly shows the reservoir on the same western valley and printed page22 independently describes its location on the river. Together these distinguish the impounded reach from an uninterrupted natural river segment and establish its upstream and downstream river connections at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Gallito Ciego retains its reservoir identity; Río Jequetepeque is not applied as a scalar replacement for the reservoir.
correspondence.managed_connection_limit: Reservoir/dam-level geography only; no surveyed intake/outlet alignment, current storage, discharge, operating state or present hydraulic performance claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Downstream river valley from Gallito Ciego into the lower coastal plain.
correspondence.finding: The map continues the same hydrographic corridor southwest and west out of the reservoir valley onto the plain. The report identifies the Talambo–Zaña intake downstream of the dam and describes its separate irrigation-channel role. The selected through-line stays in the mapped Jequetepeque river corridor to the lower westward reach rather than following the northern drainage or a different basin.
correspondence.name_scope: Bounded downstream Jequetepeque river course; no new name assigned to irrigation channels.
correspondence.managed_connection_limit: The intake’s regional setting and river continuation are established; individual gate, canal-bank or operating geometry is outside this finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lower river past the San José/Jequetepeque setting to the Pacific outlet.
correspondence.finding: The original map explicitly labels the westward selected watercourse Río Jequetepeque and traces it to the Pacific coastline north of Jequetepeque town and Pacasmayo. The separate Loco de Chamán outlet lies farther north and is not the selected terminal. The modeled sea-end extension is treated as the same ordinary coastal outlet setting, without imposing exact historical shoreline alignment.
correspondence.name_scope: Río Jequetepeque for the downstream course and terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: 61551054-headward-and-southern-course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and eastward southern course have no inspected corridor-scale cartographic match. The regional hydrographic description does not locate the selected feeder or establish its entry into a named canyon.

correspondence.component_scope: 61551054-northeast-middle-corridor
correspondence.finding: Cullen Leufú and its Mallín Chico tributary are documented in this broader region. Without the report maps, their relationship to this particular northeast-trending selection and its joins cannot be established.

correspondence.component_scope: 61551054-northern-approach-and-endpoint
correspondence.finding: The independent regional figure places Bajo de Trapalcó south of the Río Negro valley. The archaeological study documents temporary-water and spring settings there. This supports the inland terminal region, but does not trace the selected final approach through the depression or its saline/wetland joins.
